newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat eases but fails to attract buying.
newsitem.headline: German wheat eases but fails to attract buying.

text.p: German wheat export prices were marked down in a bid to attract buyers but they remained the highest in Europe, brokers said on Wednesday.
"We need export orders to revive the market, and we're looking to the EU to facilitate third country business at least along the lines of recent weeks," one said.
Brokers said the EU was under pressure to increase grain exports to relieve the internal market.
But it might be unable to offer high rebates to keep pace with falling world prices under budgetary constraints.
The Commission last Thursday cut the refund on 256,500 tonnes of wheat exports to 15.97 Ecus a tonne from 22.35.
German wheat is up to $20 a tonne more expensive than British, Danish and French origins, even after fob Baltic prices were mostly cut by 2.50 marks a tonne this week.
Normal bread wheat (12 percent protein) was offered at 280-285 marks while higher quality offers were at 285-290 and 300-302 marks, depending on protein levels.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week maintained its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 hagberg) at 280 marks/tonne and its spot feed wheat price free Hamburg at 270.
Fob rye, although little traded, was just a touch weaker at 250-262.50 marks because export demand held up and domestic consumer stocks were on the low side.
Fob barley prices also lost five marks at the top to range between 250 and 265 marks as sales to domestic and Danish feed mixers were sluggish.
